questions.q: A $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension of a number field $K$ is a Galois extension $K_\infty/K$ with Galois group:
questions.explain: By definition $\operatorname{Gal}(K_\infty/K)\cong\mathbb{Z}_p$ as topological groups; equivalently, $K_\infty=\bigcup_n K_n$ is a tower with $\operatorname{Gal}(K_n/K)\cong\mathbb{Z}/p^n\mathbb{Z}$.

questions.q: How is the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension $\mathbb{Q}_\infty$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ obtained?
choices: as the maximal real subfield of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{p^\infty})$ for $p$ odd
as the fixed field of the torsion subgroup of $\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{p^\infty})/\mathbb{Q})$
as the Hilbert class field of $\mathbb{Q}$
questions.explain: $\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{p^\infty})/\mathbb{Q})\cong\mathbb{Z}_p^\times\cong(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times\times(1+p\mathbb{Z}_p)$ for odd $p$. The torsion part $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$ has order $p-1$; the fixed field is the unique $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension.

questions.q: Iwasawa's growth formula gives $|A_n|=p^{e(n)}$ with $e(n)=\mu p^n+\lambda n+\nu$ for large $n$. If $\mu=0$, $\lambda=2$, $\nu=1$, what is $e(n)$ at $n=5$?
questions.explain: $e(5)=0\cdot p^5+2\cdot 5+1=11$. This is the linear growth regime of $\log_p|A_n|$ once $\mu=0$.

questions.q: The Iwasawa algebra is, by definition,
choices: the inverse limit $\Lambda=\varprojlim_n\mathbb{Z}_p[\Gamma/\Gamma^{p^n}]$ — the completed group algebra
questions.explain: $\Lambda=\mathbb{Z}_p[[\Gamma]]$ is the completed group algebra. Picking a topological generator $\gamma$ of $\Gamma$ and sending $\gamma\mapsto 1+T$ identifies it with the formal power series ring $\mathbb{Z}_p[[T]]$.

questions.q: The structure theorem says every finitely generated $\Lambda$-module $M$ is pseudo-isomorphic to a direct sum of cyclics. The right hand side has the form:
choices: $\Lambda^r$ alone (every finitely generated module is free up to pseudo-isomorphism)
questions.explain: A finitely generated $\Lambda$-module is pseudo-isomorphic (kernel and cokernel finite) to $\Lambda^r\oplus(\bigoplus\Lambda/(p^{a_i}))\oplus(\bigoplus\Lambda/(f_j^{m_j}))$. The torsion part lives in the latter two summands; the characteristic ideal is $(\prod p^{a_i}\cdot\prod f_j^{m_j})$.

questions.q: Which of the following are TRUE about $\Lambda=\mathbb{Z}_p[[T]]$?
choices: $\Lambda$ is a complete local ring with maximal ideal $(p,T)$
$\Lambda$ is a regular local ring of Krull dimension 2
questions.explain: $\mathbb{Z}_p[[T]]$ is a 2-dimensional regular local ring (so a UFD by Auslander–Buchsbaum), local with maximal ideal $(p,T)$. It is NOT a PID — the ideal $(p,T)$ is not principal.

questions.q: For a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-tower $K_\infty/K$, the inverse limit $X_\infty=\varprojlim A_n$ of $p$-class groups is:
questions.explain: The transition maps $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ make $X_\infty$ a $\Lambda$-module via $\Gamma$-action; Iwasawa proved it is finitely generated and torsion. Its characteristic ideal $\operatorname{char}_\Lambda X_\infty$ is the central object of the main conjecture.

questions.q: By Iwasawa's growth formula, $|A_n|=p^{\mu p^n+\lambda n+\nu}$ for $n$ large. With $\mu=1$, $\lambda=0$, $\nu=0$ and $p=3$, what is $|A_2|$?
questions.explain: $\log_3|A_2|=1\cdot 3^2+0\cdot 2+0=9$, so $|A_2|=3^9=19683$. Nonzero $\mu$ would mean class numbers blow up at $p$-adic exponential rate — Ferrero–Washington rules this out for cyclotomic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$.

questions.q: The Ferrero–Washington theorem (1979) asserts that for the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension of an abelian number field:
questions.explain: Ferrero and Washington showed the $\mu$-invariant of the minus part of $X_\infty$ vanishes for cyclotomic extensions of abelian fields. Whether $\lambda=0$ (Greenberg's conjecture, totally real case) is still open.

questions.q: The Kubota–Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-function $L_p(s,\chi)$ interpolates which classical values?
choices: $L(1-n,\chi\omega^{-n})$ at non-positive integers, multiplied by an Euler factor at $p$
the Dedekind zeta values $\zeta_K(s)$ at integers
questions.explain: $L_p(1-n,\chi)=(1-\chi\omega^{-n}(p)p^{n-1})\,L(1-n,\chi\omega^{-n})$ for $n\ge 1$. The Euler factor at $p$ is removed; the Teichmüller character $\omega$ corrects between archimedean and $p$-adic worlds.

questions.q: Why is the existence of $L_p(s,\chi)$ essentially the Kummer congruences for Bernoulli numbers?
choices: Because $L_p(s,\chi)$ is defined as the Mellin transform of a Bernoulli generating function

Because the special values $L(1-n,\chi)$ are essentially generalized Bernoulli numbers $-B_{n,\chi}/n$, and $p$-adic continuity is the Kummer congruences saying $B_{n,\chi}/n\equiv B_{m,\chi}/m\pmod{p^k}$ when $n\equiv m\pmod{(p-1)p^{k-1}}$
Because $L_p$ has no relation to Bernoulli numbers — only to class numbers
Because the Riemann hypothesis for $L_p$ is equivalent to the irrationality of $\zeta(3)$
questions.explain: Kummer's classical congruences exactly say the values $L(1-n,\chi)$ vary $p$-adically continuously in $n$ (after fixing the residue class mod $p-1$). Patching this continuity is what defines the $p$-adic $L$-function.

questions.q: Take the trivial character $\chi$ and the special value $\zeta(-1)=-1/12$. The interpolation factor at $p=5$, $n=2$ is $(1-p^{n-1})=(1-5)= -4$. What is $L_p(-1)\cdot(\text{normalisation})=(1-p)\zeta(-1)$ for $p=5$? Enter as a decimal.
questions.explain: $(1-5)(-1/12)=(-4)(-1/12)=4/12=1/3\approx 0.3333$. The factor of $(1-p^{n-1})$ removes the Euler factor at $p$; the result is the $p$-adic interpolation of $\zeta(1-n)$ at $n=2$ for the trivial character (Riemann case).

questions.q: Mazur–Wiles (1984) is the statement that — for an even Dirichlet character $\chi$ — in $\Lambda\otimes\mathbb{Q}_p$,
questions.explain: The main conjecture is the equality of two ideals in $\Lambda$: the characteristic ideal of the appropriate eigenspace of the Iwasawa module, and the ideal generated by the Kubota–Leopoldt $L_p$. Mazur–Wiles proved it for abelian $\mathbb{Q}$; Wiles for totally real fields.

questions.q: Why is the main conjecture called a 'main' conjecture?
choices: It uniformly upgrades every refined class-number formula (Stickelberger, Herbrand–Ribet, Kummer–Vandiver evidence) to a single identity of $\Lambda$-ideals.
Iwasawa happened to write it on the main blackboard at Princeton.
It is the only conjecture in Iwasawa theory.
questions.explain: Class-number formulas, Herbrand–Ribet on irregular primes, and many refined formulas are corollaries: specialising the equality of ideals at $T=0$ (or appropriate twists) recovers them. The conjecture is 'main' because everything else is a slice of it.

questions.q: Which corollaries follow from the main conjecture?
choices: Herbrand–Ribet: for $p$ irregular, $p\mid B_k$ implies the $\omega^{1-k}$-eigenspace of $X_\infty$ is non-trivial
the leading-term formula $\zeta_p(K,1-n)\doteq h_n^-/(\text{regulator})$ relating $p$-adic $L$-values to class numbers
the analytic continuation of the classical Riemann zeta to $\mathbb{C}$
questions.explain: Herbrand–Ribet and refined class-number formulas drop out; analytic continuation of $\zeta(s)$ predates Iwasawa theory and FLT requires the modularity theorem (a different machine, although Iwasawa-flavoured deformation theory plays a role).

questions.q: For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ with good ordinary reduction at $p$, the elliptic Iwasawa main conjecture predicts:
choices: $\Lambda$ acts trivially on the Selmer group
questions.explain: The dual Selmer group is a finitely generated torsion $\Lambda$-module; the main conjecture equates its characteristic ideal with the ideal generated by the $p$-adic $L$-function $L_p(E,T)$ of Mazur–Swinnerton-Dyer.

questions.q: The Coates–Wiles theorem (1977) was the first major application of Iwasawa methods to BSD; it states:
choices: If $E$ has CM by an imaginary quadratic field and $L(E,1)\ne 0$, then $E(\mathbb{Q})$ is finite.
Every elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ is modular.
questions.explain: Coates–Wiles: if $E/\mathbb{Q}$ has complex multiplication and $L(E,1)\ne 0$, then $E(\mathbb{Q})$ has rank zero. This is one direction of weak BSD in the CM case, proved by descent along the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension.

questions.q: Which contributions form the modern proof of (one direction of) the elliptic main conjecture for many ordinary $E/\mathbb{Q}$?
choices: Kato's Euler system, giving one divisibility $\operatorname{char}\mid L_p$
Skinner–Urban's converse via Eisenstein congruences on $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)$, giving $L_p\mid\operatorname{char}$
the modularity theorem (Wiles, Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor) supplying the modular forms input
questions.explain: Kato (Euler systems on Beilinson elements), Skinner–Urban (Eisenstein-congruence side), and modularity (so that $E$ corresponds to a newform feeding into the construction) together give $p$-part BSD for many curves of analytic rank $\le 1$. RH plays no role.
